text:
Sam: Heads-up — ClearHarbor renewal in 14 days. AM reports a steep drop in feature usage and they mentioned they're evaluating a lower-cost plan if we can't address instability. Opening thread to scope a "stabilization sprint" and soft-landing options. :thinking:
Priya: Saw their telemetry. Spike in error-rate and some auth token refresh failures after our identity rollout two weeks ago. Not full outage but enough to degrade UX.
Carlos: I dug into logs: `403 token_refresh_failed` ~ 120 events/day last 10 days. Also a pair of spikes where p95 latency doubled during batch jobs.
Leah: Customer is mid-market but recently ramped usage. Suggest a two-track save: 1) immediate tech stabilizers we can run quickly, 2) a downgrade cushion offer so they don't churn while we fix.
Sam: Concrete proposal:
- Tech stabilizers (48-72h): rollback identity config toggle for their tenant OR apply token refresh retry backoff + hotfix. Enable a temporary traffic-split to stable runtime variant.
- Enablement: 60m integration deep-dive (CS + Eng) to run a short validation harness and confirm token lifecycle.
- Commercial "soft-landing": offer a downgrade cushion: allow one-month downgrade at current committed seat price (no penalty) if they need to move down during the stabilization window; if they stay, no chargebacks.
Priya: I can draft the technical instructions and the validation checklist. Will include curl examples to refresh tokens and a small script to simulate refresh storms.
Carlos: Draft of reproduction command I used:
```
# simulate token refresh storm
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.dev/v1/tokens/refresh -d '{"tenant":"clearharbor"}' & done
```
Leah: Commercial note: Finance ok with a single-month downgrade cushion as long as we limit to customers with <10k monthly spend and get legal to sign off on terms. I'll ping Maya.
Sam: Owners + timeline:
- Priya: technical runbook + validation checklist (ETA: today EOD).
- Carlos: run canary traffic-split to stable runtime and monitor 1h/6h p95 + error rate (ETA: tomorrow morning).
- Leah: draft commercial cushion terms + send to Maya for approval (ETA: today afternoon).
- Sam: draft customer email explaining the plan and options (ETA: today night).
Priya: I'll also prepare a mini SDK snippet to surface retries client-side in case they need a quick fix while we patch the backend.
Carlos: Can we auto-instrument a short perf dashboard slice for them? I'll create a Velox-like dashboard and share a read-only link.
OpsBot: Dashboard created: https://dash.redwood/clearharbor/stabilization-14d. Auto-alert configured for error-rate > 0.8%.
Leah: Communication approach: transparent but calm. "We're rolling a focused stabilization sprint for your tenant over the next 72 hours; we'll run tests with you and offer a one-month downgrade cushion while we validate improvements."
Sam: Agreed. Priya, attach the validation checklist to the customer invite. Carlos, do the canary only during the enablement slot so we can show live improvements.
Priya: Checklist will include: token-refresh log locations, sample requests, expected p50/p95 ranges, and a brief guide to client retry knobs.
Carlos: I'll post rollback commands in thread 15m before canary.
Leah: If they accept, we should also schedule a survey 48h post-fix to capture sentiment: perceived reliability, remaining blockers, and willingness to renew at current terms.
OpsBot: Survey template created: https://rdw-internal/surveys/clearharbor-stab. Will send 48h after fix.
Sam: Good. Let's keep this lightweight and timebox to 72h. If we make no measurable progress, we agree escalation to an executive check-in and a targeted discount discussion.
Priya: Starting work now. Posting runbook in thread when ready.
Carlos: Willing to support the enablement session tomorrow afternoon.
Leah: I'll loop Maya and legal after I finish the draft terms.
Sam: Thanks team. If you hit blockers, ping @sam. We'll reconvene after the enablement and the survey. :thumbsup:
